issues.title: Quantum \(6j\)-summand update ratio
issues.failure_explanation: For an interior update z_min <= z < z_max and generic q where the quotient is defined, dividing the Racah summand at z+1 by that at z changes the sign, contributes [z+2]_q from the numerator factorial, contributes 1/[z+1-a_i]_q for each a_i denominator factorial, and contributes [b_y-z]_q for each b_y denominator factorial. Thus the quotient is -[z+2]_q times the product of the b_y-z factors divided by the product of the z+1-a_i factors. The old equation reverses those product roles and shifts each b_y factor incorrectly. Moreover, at z=z_max-1, any y attaining b_y=z_max makes its old denominator contain [0]_q, so the literal old update is undefined for every nontrivial summation range.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm alg:compilation generally fails to track the Racah summands after the base term and encounters an identically zero denominator in its final update for a nontrivial range. Consequently, the resulting quantum-6j DCR and the application of prop:deformation_as_evaluation to that construction are not established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace eq:ratio_Rz by \(\mathcal R_z=-[z+2]_q\,\prod_{y=1}^3[b_y-z]_q/\prod_{i=1}^4[z+1-a_i]_q\) for \(z_{\min}\le z<z_{\max}\), and use this corrected ratio in the compilation updates and the termwise construction underlying prop:deformation_as_evaluation. This restores \(\mathcal M_{z+1}=\mathcal M_z\mathcal R_z\).
issues.why_classification: The quotient follows by a short, routine local cancellation of consecutive factorials in eq:racah_6j, and correcting it preserves the DCR construction and dependent proposition without a new lemma, architectural change, or weakened guarantee. It is not merely a typo because the compilation algorithm actually consumes the erroneous recurrence, producing incorrect and sometimes undefined updates.

issues.title: Projection parameter and input contract

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This object encodes the full algebraic structure of the series independently of any numerical value of $q$.

issues.failure_explanation: The old algorithm's inputs do not determine its output. For example, in the same target field C, the valid cyclotomic monomial with sign 1, P=1, and all cyclotomic exponents zero evaluates to 2 when q=2 and to 3 when q=3. Both use the identical declared field input, while the parameter-independent DCR contains neither choice. In addition, because P may be negative, the image of q must be nonzero. Thus a target field by itself determines neither q^P nor the values Phi_d(q^2), and the old projection procedure lacks a required evaluation datum.
issues.overall_effect: For generic real, complex, or repeated-parameter evaluation, alg:projection is not a function of its declared inputs and cannot guarantee the stated evaluated amplitude. The parameter-independent compilation stage itself is unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require, in addition to the DCR, a specified admissible nonzero evaluation element \(q\in\mathbb K^\times\) in the target field (equivalently, an evaluation homomorphism assigning the formal parameter). Define the projection using that datum, evaluate \(q^P\) and every \(\Phi_d(q^2)\) from it, and state the output as \(S(q)\in\mathbb K\).
issues.why_classification: This is a genuine underdetermined-input defect, not a transcriptional typo, because a target field alone does not specify the values used by the algorithm. Supplying the evaluation element or homomorphism is nevertheless a short, routine local contract repair that leaves the parameter-independent compilation, evaluated amplitude, applicability to the intended regimes, and complexity guarantees unchanged.
